pages.title: Cellular Respiration
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

   Cellular Respiration



⬣   Cellular respiration is a process by which the pyruvate produced
    by glycolysis is further oxidized to H2O and CO2

           - Used by animals, plants, and many microorganisms
           - Provides more energy (ATP) from glucose than glycolysis
           - Also captures energy stored in lipids and amino           acids


⬣   Occurs in three major stages       :

           - Acetyl CoA production
           - Acetyl CoA oxidation
           - Electron transfer and oxidative phosphorylation

concepts.label: Cellular respiration and energy capture
concepts.detail: Pyruvate from glycolysis is further oxidized to H2O and CO2; used by animals, plants and many microorganisms; provides more ATP from glucose than glycolysis and captures energy in lipids and amino acids.

concepts.label: Three stages of cellular respiration
concepts.detail: The stated order is acetyl-CoA production, acetyl-CoA oxidation, then electron transfer and oxidative phosphorylation.

pages.title: Conversion of Pyruvate to Acetyl-CoA
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Conversion of Pyruvate to Acetyl-CoA



                                                                    ⬣   Oxidative decarboxylation of
                                                                        pyruvate is an irreversible
                                                                        oxidation process in which the
                                                                        carboxyl group is removed,
                                                                        forming CO2 and acetyl-CoA


                                                                    ⬣   Catalyzed by the pyruvate
                                                                        dehydrogenase complex


                                                                    ⬣   Requires five cofactors, four of
                                                                        which are derived from vitamins.
pages.visualNotes: Reaction: pyruvate + CoA-SH + NAD+ → acetyl-CoA + CO2 + NADH. Enzyme label: pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (E1 + E2 + E3); auxiliary labels TPP, lipoate, FAD; ΔG′° = −33.4 kJ/mol. The removed pyruvate carboxyl is highlighted.

concepts.label: PDH oxidative decarboxylation
concepts.detail: Pyruvate undergoes irreversible oxidative decarboxylation to CO2 and acetyl-CoA, catalyzed by PDH complex; NAD+ is reduced to NADH.

concepts.label: PDH cofactor requirement
concepts.detail: Five cofactors are required; four are vitamin-derived.

pages.title: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (PDH)
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
           Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (PDH)


⬣   The PDH is a large multienzyme       Complex Employs Three Enzymes and Five
    Coenzymes to Oxidize Pyruvate


⬣   Contains multiple copies of three enzymes
          - Pyruvate dehydrogenase (E1)
          - Dihydrolipoyl   transacetylase   (E2)
          - Dihydrolipoyl   dehydrogenase (E3)


⬣   Requires five different coenzymes or prosthetic groups
          - Lipoate  (lipoicacid)
          - Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) derived from vitamin (B1)
          - Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) derived from vitamin (B2)
          - Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) derived from vitamin (B3)
          - Coenzyme A (CoA, CoA-SH) derived from vitamin (B5)

concepts.label: Three enzymes of PDH
concepts.detail: PDH contains multiple copies of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1, dihydrolipoyl transacetylase E2 and dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase E3.

concepts.label: Five PDH coenzymes and vitamin origins
concepts.detail: Lipoate/lipoic acid; TPP from B1; FAD from B2; NAD from B3; CoA/CoA-SH from B5.

pages.title: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate by the PDH complex
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate by the PDH complex
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
   Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate by the PDH complex

⬣   Enzyme 1
    Step 1: Decarboxylation of pyruvate to the
    hydroxyethyl derivative
    Step 2: Oxidation of the hydroxyethyl derivative to
    an acetyl group
            ‒ Electrons and the acetyl group are
transferred from TPP to the lipoyllysyl   group of E2

⬣   Enzyme 2
   Step 3: Formation of acetyl-CoA (product 1)

⬣   Enzyme 3
    Step 4: Electron transfer to regenerate the oxidized
    form of the lipoyllysyl  group

   Step 5: Regeneration of the oxidized FAD cofactor
            ‒ Forming NADH (product 2)
pages.visualNotes: Five-step figure labels: pyruvate; CO2; TPP; hydroxyethyl TPP; acetyl lipoyllysine; oxidized lipoyllysine (S−S); reduced lipoyllysine (SH/SH); CoA-SH; acetyl-CoA; Lys; FAD; FADH2; NAD+; NADH + H+. Domains E1 pyruvate dehydrogenase, E2 dihydrolipoyl transacetylase, E3 dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase. Arrows carry hydroxyethyl/acetyl group via swinging lipoyllysine, then electrons to FAD and NAD+.

concepts.label: E1 decarboxylation and acetyl transfer
concepts.detail: E1 step1 decarboxylates pyruvate to hydroxyethyl derivative; step2 oxidizes this derivative to acetyl group and transfers electrons/acetyl from TPP to E2 lipoyllysyl group.

concepts.label: E2 forms acetyl-CoA
concepts.detail: E2 step3 forms acetyl-CoA, labeled product1.

concepts.label: E3 regenerates oxidized cofactors
concepts.detail: E3 step4 transfers electrons to regenerate oxidized lipoyllysyl group; step5 regenerates oxidized FAD while producing NADH, product2.

pages.title: Regulation of Pyruvate dehydrogenase Complex
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
            Regulation of Pyruvate dehydrogenase Complex


⬣   The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDH) is regulated through a combination of covalent
    modification and allosteric mechanisms


⬣   The PDH complex in mammals is allosterically inhibited by ATP, acetyl-CoA, and NADH


⬣    AMP, CoA, and NAD+, which accumulate when acetate flow into the citric acid cycle is
    insufficient, allosterically  activates the PDH complex      .


⬣   High levels of ATP and NADH, indicative of sufficient energy production, inhibit the PDH
    complex, slowing down pyruvate decarboxylation            .


⬣   Elevated levels of ADP and calcium ions activate the complex, promoting the conversion of
    pyruvate to acetyl   -CoA when more energy is needed

concepts.label: Covalent and allosteric PDH regulation
concepts.detail: PDH regulation combines covalent modification and allosteric mechanisms.

concepts.label: High-energy PDH inhibition
concepts.detail: ATP, acetyl-CoA and NADH allosterically inhibit mammalian PDH; high ATP and NADH signal sufficient energy and slow pyruvate decarboxylation.

concepts.label: Low-energy/need-related PDH activation
concepts.detail: AMP, CoA and NAD+ activate PDH when acetate flow into TCA is insufficient; elevated ADP and calcium activate conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA when energy is needed.

Regulation of Pyruvate dehydrogenase Complex

concepts.label: PDH phosphatase and calcium activate
concepts.detail: PDH phosphatase uses H2O, releases Pi and produces active PDH; Ca++ signals sudden cellular demand and promotes activation.

pages.title: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency


    ⬣   Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency is a rare genetic mitochondrial disorder that
        results from mutations in the genes encoding components of the PDH complex,
        leading to a dysfunctional enzyme.


    ⬣   PDH deficiency is most commonly linked to the alpha unit of E1, which is X-linked,
        but autosomal recessive variants also exist.


    ⬣   It causes elevated serum lactate, pyruvate and alanine.


    ⬣   Associated with lactic acidosis, progressive neurological and neuromuscular
        degeneration, and, usually, death during childhood.

concepts.label: PDH deficiency genetics
concepts.detail: Rare genetic mitochondrial disorder caused by mutations in PDH component genes; most commonly E1 alpha unit, X-linked; autosomal-recessive variants also exist.

concepts.label: PDH deficiency biochemical/clinical effects
concepts.detail: Elevated serum lactate, pyruvate and alanine; lactic acidosis, progressive neurological/neuromuscular degeneration and usually death during childhood.

pages.title: Therapeutic Approaches for PDH Deficiency
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Therapeutic Approaches for PDH Deficiency


⬣   Use of a ketogenic diet:

          - High-fat, adequate protein, low-carb diet.
          - Forces the body to prioritize fat metabolism.
          - Mitigates metabolic challenges in PDH Deficiency.


⬣   Dichloroacetic    Acid (DCA):

          - Investigated for treating lactic acidosis in PDH Deficiency.
          - Stimulates pyruvate dehydrogenase activity.
          - Inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase.
          - Shifts metabolism toward mitochondrial oxidation,
          reducing lactate production.
pages.visualNotes: Chemical figure labeled Dichloroacetate shows two Cl substituents on CH attached to a carboxylate.

concepts.label: Ketogenic diet in PDH deficiency
concepts.detail: High fat, adequate protein, low carbohydrate diet prioritizes fat metabolism and mitigates metabolic challenges.

concepts.label: Dichloroacetate mechanism in PDH deficiency
concepts.detail: Dichloroacetic acid (DCA) is investigated for lactic acidosis; stimulates PDH, inhibits PDH kinase, shifts toward mitochondrial oxidation and reduces lactate production.

pages.title: Thiamin (Vitamin B1) deficiency causes Beriberi
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Thiamin (Vitamin B1) deficiency causes Beriberi



  ⬣   Thiamine is an essential dietary requirement for most vertebrates.


  ⬣   Most vertebrates do not synthesize or store thiamine in significant amounts.


  ⬣   Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) serves as a crucial coenzyme for the pyruvate
      dehydrogenase complex (PDH) in glucose metabolism.


  ⬣   Thiamine deficiency leads to Beriberi, a fatal disease, that is characterized by neurological
      disturbances, paralysis, limb atrophy, and cardiac failure.


  ⬣   Beriberi is rare in developed countries due to vitamin-enriched foods. It is more prevalent in
      individuals who abuse alcohol, as excess alcohol impairs thiamine absorption and storage,
      leading to poor nutrition.

concepts.label: Thiamine intake and TPP
concepts.detail: Thiamine is essential in most vertebrates, which do not synthesize/store significant amounts; TPP is crucial PDH coenzyme in glucose metabolism.

concepts.label: Thiamine deficiency and Beriberi
concepts.detail: Source calls Beriberi fatal and lists neurological disturbances, paralysis, limb atrophy and cardiac failure; rare in developed countries with vitamin-enriched foods; alcohol abuse impairs absorption/storage and causes poor nutrition.

pages.title: Reactions of the Citric Acid Cycle
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Reactions of the Citric Acid Cycle
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
           Reactions of the
            Citric Acid Cycle


⬣   In each cycle turn, one acetyl group enters
    as acetyl-CoA, and two molecules of CO2
    are released.

⬣   One molecule of oxaloacetate is used to
    form citrate, and one is regenerated.


⬣   Four of the eight steps involve oxidations,
    conserving energy in the form of NADH
    and FADH2.

⬣   NADH and FADH2 donate electrons to the
    respiratory chain, driving ATP synthesis.
pages.visualNotes: Full labeled cycle: 1 aldol condensation; 2a dehydration and 2b rehydration reposition citrate OH in isocitrate to set up next decarboxylation; 3 oxidative decarboxylation, OH oxidized to carbonyl and CO2 lost; 4 oxidative decarboxylation with PDH-like mechanism dependent on carbonyl on adjacent carbon; 5 substrate-level phosphorylation, thioester energy conserved in GTP/ATP phosphoanhydride; 6 dehydrogenation introduces double bond and initiates methylene oxidation sequence; 7 hydration introduces OH for next oxidation; 8 OH dehydrogenation gives carbonyl positioned for aldol condensation. NADH at isocitrate, α-ketoglutarate and malate steps; FADH2 at succinate step; GTP/ATP at succinyl-CoA step; two CO2 at steps3 and4; CoA-SH at step1 and5; CoA-SH entry at step4.

concepts.label: Cycle entry, CO2 and oxaloacetate regeneration
concepts.detail: Each turn takes one acetyl group as acetyl-CoA, releases two CO2, uses one oxaloacetate to make citrate and regenerates one oxaloacetate.

concepts.label: Four oxidation steps conserve energy
concepts.detail: Four of eight steps oxidize substrates and conserve energy in NADH/FADH2; those carriers donate to respiratory chain and drive ATP synthesis.

concepts.label: Citric acid cycle sequence and enzymes
concepts.detail: Citrate synthase: OAA+acetyl-CoA→citrate; aconitase: citrate↔cis-aconitate↔isocitrate; isocitrate dehydrogenase→α-ketoglutarate; α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase→succinyl-CoA; succinyl-CoA synthetase→succinate; succinate dehydrogenase→fumarate; fumarase→malate; malate dehydrogenase→OAA.

pages.title: Formation of Citrate
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Formation of Citrate



  ⬣   Citrate synthase catalyzes the condensation of acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetate to form citrate
             - Involves the formation of a transient intermediate, citroyl-CoA
             - Large, negative ∆G′°    is needed because [oxaloacetate] is normally very low
pages.visualNotes: Reaction drawing: acetyl-CoA + oxaloacetate + H2O → citrate + CoA-SH, catalyzed by citrate synthase; ΔG′° = −32.2 kJ/mol.

concepts.label: Citrate synthase condensation
concepts.detail: Acetyl-CoA condenses with oxaloacetate to citrate through transient citroyl-CoA; large negative ΔG′° matters because OAA concentration is normally very low.

pages.title: Induced Fit in the Citrate Synthase
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Induced Fit in the Citrate Synthase
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Induced Fit in the Citrate Synthase



 ⬣    Binding of oxaloacetate causes a conformational
      change creating a binding site for acetyl-CoA


        ○    Open conformation:
             Free enzyme does not have a binding site for
             acetyl-CoA.
        ○    Closed conformation:
             Binding of OAA creates binding for acetyl-CoA.


 ⬣    Induced fit decreases the likelihood of premature
      cleavage of the thioester bond of acetyl-CoA
pages.visualNotes: Two enzyme structures show open and closed conformations; labels oxaloacetate and acetyl-CoA analog. OAA-bound structure closes around binding site.

concepts.label: Ordered binding and citrate synthase induced fit
concepts.detail: Free/open enzyme lacks acetyl-CoA binding site; OAA binding creates closed conformation and acetyl-CoA site; induced fit reduces premature cleavage of acetyl-CoA thioester bond.

pages.title: Formation of Isocitrate via Cis-Aconitate
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

      Formation of Isocitrate via Cis-Aconitate



⬣   Aconitase   (aconitate   hydratase)
    catalyzes the reversible transformation
    of citrate to isocitrate  through the
    intermediate cis-aconitate

           -Addition of H2O to cis-aconitate
           is stereospecific
           -Low [isocitrate] pulls the
           reaction forward
pages.visualNotes: Structural reaction drawing: citrate ⇌ cis-aconitate + H2O; cis-aconitate + H2O ⇌ isocitrate, both aconitase. Hydroxyl position changes; ΔG′° = 13.3 kJ/mol.

concepts.label: Aconitase isomerization via cis-aconitate
concepts.detail: Aconitase/aconitate hydratase reversibly converts citrate to isocitrate through cis-aconitate; water addition stereospecific; low isocitrate pulls forward.

pages.title: Oxidation of Isocitrate to α-Ketoglutarate and CO2
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Oxidation of Isocitrate to α-Ketoglutarate and CO2
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

  Oxidation of Isocitrate                     to α-Ketoglutarate                    and CO2



⬣   Isocitrate dehydrogenase catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate           to α-ketoglutarate

          - Mn2+ interacts with the carbonyl group of the        oxalosuccinate    and stabilizes the
          transiently-formed enol
          - Specific isozymes for NADP+ (cytosolic and mitochondrial) or NAD+ (mitochondrial)
pages.visualNotes: Three-part mechanism: 1 hydride transfer to NAD+ or NADP+ depending on isozyme creates oxalosuccinate, NAD(P)H+H+; 2 adjacent carbonyl and coordinated Mn2+ facilitate CO2 loss/electron withdrawal; 3 enol rearrangement regenerates α-ketoglutarate.

concepts.label: Isocitrate oxidative decarboxylation
concepts.detail: Isocitrate dehydrogenase converts isocitrate to α-ketoglutarate with CO2 release; Mn2+ interacts with oxalosuccinate carbonyl and stabilizes transient enol.

concepts.label: NAD versus NADP isocitrate dehydrogenase isozymes
concepts.detail: NADP+-specific isozymes are cytosolic and mitochondrial; NAD+-specific form is mitochondrial.

pages.title: Oxidation of α-Ketoglutarate to Succinyl-CoA and CO2
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Oxidation of α-Ketoglutarate to Succinyl-CoA and CO2
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Oxidation of α-Ketoglutarate                       to Succinyl-CoA and CO2


    ⬣   α-ketoglutarate   dehydrogenase complex catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of α-
        ketoglutarate   to succinyl-CoA and CO2

              -Energy of oxidation is conserved in the thioester bond of succinyl-CoA
pages.visualNotes: Reaction: α-ketoglutarate + CoA-SH + NAD+ → succinyl-CoA + CO2 + NADH; ΔG′° = −33.5 kJ/mol.

concepts.label: α-Ketoglutarate oxidative decarboxylation
concepts.detail: α-Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex makes succinyl-CoA and CO2; oxidation energy conserved in succinyl-CoA thioester.

pages.title: Conversion of Succinyl-CoA to Succinate
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Conversion of Succinyl-CoA to Succinate


 ⬣    Succinyl-CoA synthetase     (succinic thiokinase) catalyzes the breakage of the thioester bond
      of succinyl-CoA to form succinate
            - Energy released drives the synthesis of a phosphoanhydride           bond in either GTP or
            ATP (substrate level phosphorylation)
pages.visualNotes: Reaction drawing: succinyl-CoA + GDP + Pi ⇌ succinate + GTP + CoA-SH; ΔG′° = −2.9 kJ/mol. Text explicitly allows GTP or ATP.

concepts.label: Succinyl-CoA substrate-level phosphorylation
concepts.detail: Succinyl-CoA synthetase/succinic thiokinase breaks thioester to succinate; energy drives GTP or ATP phosphoanhydride formation by substrate-level phosphorylation.

pages.title: Oxidation of Succinate to Fumarate
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Oxidation of Succinate to Fumarate

 ⬣    Succinate dehydrogenase is a flavoprotein        that catalyzes the reversible oxidation of
      succinate to fumarate
            - Integral protein of the mitochondrial inner membrane in eukaryotes
            - Contains three iron-sulfur clusters and covalently bound FAD
pages.visualNotes: Reaction drawing: succinate + FAD ⇌ fumarate + FADH2 via succinate dehydrogenase; ΔG′° = 0 kJ/mol. Separate molecular structures labeled malonate and succinate are shown side by side; no inhibitory relationship is explicitly labeled here, so no such relationship is added.

concepts.label: Succinate dehydrogenase location/cofactor
concepts.detail: Flavoprotein reversibly oxidizes succinate to fumarate; eukaryotic mitochondrial inner-membrane integral protein; three Fe-S clusters and covalently bound FAD.

pages.title: Hydration of Fumarate to Malate
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

      Hydration of Fumarate to Malate




⬣   Fumarase   catalyzes the
    reversible hydration of
    fumarate to L-malate

-Transition state is a carbanion
pages.visualNotes: Mechanism drawing: fumarate + OH− → carbanion transition state; H+ addition gives L-malate. Separate structures label fumarate, L-malate and D-malate. ΔG′° = −3.8 kJ/mol.

concepts.label: Fumarase stereospecific hydration
concepts.detail: Fumarase reversibly hydrates fumarate to L-malate; transition state is carbanion.

pages.title: Oxidation of Malate to Oxaloacetate
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

    Oxidation of Malate to Oxaloacetate

⬣   L-malate dehydrogenase catalyzes the oxidation of  L-malate to oxaloacetate, coupled to
    the reduction of NAD+

          - Low [oxaloacetate] pulls the reaction forward
          - Regenerates oxaloacetate for citrate synthesis
pages.visualNotes: Reaction drawing: L-malate + NAD+ ⇌ oxaloacetate + NADH + H+; ΔG′° = 29.7 kJ/mol.

concepts.label: Malate dehydrogenase and OAA pull
concepts.detail: L-malate dehydrogenase oxidizes L-malate to oxaloacetate with NAD+ reduction; low OAA pulls forward and regenerated OAA serves citrate synthesis.

pages.title: Net Result of the Citric Acid Cycle
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Net Result of the Citric Acid Cycle
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Net Result of the Citric Acid Cycle



 ⬣   Net oxidation of two carbons to CO2


 ⬣   The energy released by oxidation is
     conserved in the production of:


    3 NADH
    1 FADH2


 ⬣   Generates 1 GTP, which can be
     converted to ATP


Acetyl-CoA + 3NAD+ + FAD + GDP + Pi + 2 H2O 
2CO2 + 3NADH + FADH2 + GTP + CoA + 3H+
pages.visualNotes: Net equation as printed: Acetyl-CoA + 3NAD+ + FAD + GDP + Pi + 2 H2O → 2CO2 + 3NADH + FADH2 + GTP + CoA + 3H+. Cycle diagram positions NADH at isocitrate→α-ketoglutarate, α-ketoglutarate→succinyl-CoA and malate→OAA; FADH2 at succinate→fumarate; GTP(ATP) at succinyl-CoA→succinate.

concepts.label: Net TCA products per acetyl-CoA
concepts.detail: Net oxidation of two carbons to CO2; 3 NADH, 1 FADH2 and 1 GTP, convertible to ATP; CoA and 3 H+ also appear in stated net equation.

pages.title: Summary
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
                           Summary



⬣   Acetyl-CoA initiates the cycle by donating its acetyl group to oxaloacetate, forming citrate, a six-carbon
    compound.
⬣   Citrate is converted into isocitrate, another six-carbon molecule. Dehydrogenation of isocitrate, with
    the loss of CO2, produces α-ketoglutarate, a five-carbon compound.
⬣   α-Ketoglutarate     undergoes further decarboxylation, losing a second CO2 molecule, ultimately yielding
    succinate, a four-carbon compound.
⬣   Succinate is enzymatically converted in three steps into oxaloacetate, completing the cycle.
⬣   Each cycle turnover involves the entry of one acetyl group (two carbons) from acetyl-CoA. Two
    molecules of CO2 are released. One molecule of oxaloacetate is used to form citrate, and one molecule
    is regenerated, ensuring no net removal of oxaloacetate.
⬣   Four of the eight steps in the cycle are oxidation reactions, leading to the efficient conservation of
    energy in the form of reduced coenzymes NADH and FADH2.
⬣   Oxaloacetate is present in cells in very low concentrations, allowing it theoretically to participate in the
    oxidation of numerous acetyl groups.
pages.visualNotes: The summary restates one acetyl group/two CO2 per turnover, four oxidation reactions of eight steps conserving NADH/FADH2, and very low cellular OAA permitting repeated acetyl-group oxidation.

concepts.label: Carbon counts through the TCA cycle
concepts.detail: Acetyl-CoA donates two-carbon group to OAA to form six-carbon citrate; six-carbon isocitrate loses CO2 to five-carbon α-ketoglutarate; further decarboxylation ultimately yields four-carbon succinate; three steps convert succinate to OAA. One OAA used and regenerated without net removal.

pages.title: Role of the Citric Acid Cycle in Anabolism
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
topics: Role of the Citric Acid Cycle in Anabolism
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
     Role of the Citric Acid
     Cycle in Anabolism


⬣   The citric acid cycle serves both catabolic and
    anabolic processes in aerobic organisms.


⬣   Oxaloacetate and α-ketoglutarate       serve as
    precursors for aspartate and glutamate
    through simple transamination.


⬣   Succinyl-CoA, is crucial for synthesizing the
    porphyrin ring of heme     groups.

⬣   Oxaloacetate from the cycle can be
    converted to glucose through
    gluconeogenesis.
pages.visualNotes: Anabolic diagram: OAA ↔ phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), labeled PEP carboxykinase on outward arrow and PEP carboxylase on return; PEP → glucose and serine/glycine/cysteine/phenylalanine/tyrosine/tryptophan. OAA → aspartate/asparagine → pyrimidines. Citrate → fatty acids/sterols. α-Ketoglutarate → glutamate → glutamine/proline/arginine and purines. Succinyl-CoA → porphyrins/heme. Red replenishing arrows: pyruvate → OAA (pyruvate carboxylase), PEP → OAA (PEP carboxylase), pyruvate → malate (malic enzyme).

concepts.label: Catabolic and anabolic TCA roles
concepts.detail: TCA serves both catabolic and anabolic processes in aerobic organisms.

concepts.label: TCA intermediates as biosynthetic precursors
concepts.detail: OAA and α-ketoglutarate become aspartate and glutamate by transamination; succinyl-CoA supplies heme porphyrin ring; OAA can support glucose formation through gluconeogenesis.

concepts.rationale: Source detail retained without mandatory assessment emphasis; table authoring waits for owner where stated.
concepts.detail: Diagram connects citrate to fatty acids/sterols; α-ketoglutarate through glutamate to glutamine/proline/arginine and purines; OAA through aspartate/asparagine to pyrimidines; PEP to serine/glycine/cysteine/phenylalanine/tyrosine/tryptophan; succinyl-CoA to porphyrins/heme.

pages.title: Anaplerotic Reactions
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
                      Anaplerotic                Reactions


⬣    Intermediates in the citric acid cycle can be used in biosynthetic pathways (removed from cycle).

⬣    Must replenish the intermediates in order for          the cycle and central metabolic pathway to          continue


⬣    The most important anaplerotic        reaction in mammalian liver, kidney, and brown adipose tissue is
     the reversible carboxylation of pyruvate        to form oxaloacetate, catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase.
pages.visualNotes: TABLE16-2, Anaplerotic Reactions, columns Reaction and Tissue(s)/organism(s). Row1: Pyruvate + HCO3− + ATP ⇌ oxaloacetate + ADP + Pi; pyruvate carboxylase; liver, kidney. Row2: phosphoenolpyruvate + CO2 + GDP ⇌ oxaloacetate + GTP; PEP carboxykinase; heart, skeletal muscle. Row3: phosphoenolpyruvate + HCO3− ⇌ oxaloacetate + Pi; PEP carboxylase; higher plants, yeast, bacteria. Row4: pyruvate + HCO3− + NAD(P)H ⇌ malate + NAD(P)+; malic enzyme; widely distributed in eukaryotes and bacteria. Arrows are preserved as drawn, without validating their biochemical reversibility. Table material is preserved for source fidelity; questions/Memorize on table-only facts wait for the owner’s choice.

concepts.detail: TCA intermediates removed for biosynthesis must be replenished for cycle/central metabolism to continue.

pages.title: Citric Acid Cycle Regulation
pages.visualReviewer: Codex chapter writer; source inspection, not independent review
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

   Citric Acid Cycle Regulation



⬣   Regulation balances the supply of key
    intermediates with the demands of energy
    production and biosynthetic processes


⬣   Regulation occurs at several points:

          - PDH complex
          - Citrate synthase
          - Isocitrate dehydrogenase complex
          - α-ketoglutarate    dehydrogenase complex
pages.visualNotes: Regulation diagram names all cycle intermediates/enzymes and energy products as on p27, with red inhibition symbols and green activation symbols. PDH: ATP, acetyl-CoA, NADH, fatty acids inhibit; AMP, CoA, NAD+, Ca2+ activate. Citrate synthase: NADH, succinyl-CoA, citrate, ATP inhibit; ADP activates. Isocitrate dehydrogenase: ATP inhibits; Ca2+, ADP activate. α-Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase: succinyl-CoA and NADH inhibit; Ca2+ activates.

concepts.label: Regulation balances energy and biosynthesis
concepts.detail: Regulation balances intermediate supply against energy and biosynthetic demand; regulatory points PDH, citrate synthase, isocitrate dehydrogenase complex and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex.

concepts.label: Regulatory effectors in pathway diagram
concepts.detail: PDH inhibited ATP/acetyl-CoA/NADH/fatty acids, activated AMP/CoA/NAD+/Ca2+; citrate synthase inhibited NADH/succinyl-CoA/citrate/ATP, activated ADP; isocitrate dehydrogenase inhibited ATP, activated Ca2+/ADP; α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase inhibited succinyl-CoA/NADH, activated Ca2+.
